requirements.subject: ent:array
requirements.canonical: An array IS a shorthand notation to specify a record of type.
requirements.original: Arrays can be used in TTCN-3 as a shorthand notation to specify record of types.

requirements.subject: ent:array
requirements.canonical: An array MAY be specified at the point of a variable declaration, formal parameter declaration or function return value declaration.
requirements.original: They may be specified also at the point of a variable, formal parameter or function return value declaration.

requirements.subject: ent:array
requirements.canonical: An array MAY be declared as single-dimensional or multi-dimensional.
requirements.original: Arrays may be declared as single or multi-dimensional.

requirements.subject: ent:array-dimension
requirements.canonical: An array dimension SHALL be specified using a constant expression.
requirements.original: Array dimensions shall be specified using constant expressions, which shall evaluate to a positive integer values.

requirements.subject: ent:constant-expression
requirements.canonical: A constant expression specifying an array dimension SHALL evaluate to a positive integer value.
requirements.original: Array dimensions shall be specified using constant expressions, which shall evaluate to a positive integer values.

requirements.subject: ent:constant
requirements.canonical: A constant used in a constant expression specifying an array dimension SHALL meet the restrictions of clause 10.
requirements.original: Constants used in the constant expressions shall meet with the restrictions in clause 10.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: An array element IS accessed by means of the index notation ([]).
requirements.original: Array elements are accessed by means of the index notation ([]), which shall specify a valid index within the array's range.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: The index notation used to access an array element SHALL specify a valid index within the array's range.
requirements.original: Array elements are accessed by means of the index notation ([]), which shall specify a valid index within the array's range.

ambiguity.issue: Source unit is classified as example-text by the PDF conversion although it is normative prose following an example; normative is set to false per extraction rules.

requirements.subject: ent:array-element
requirements.canonical: An individual element of a multi-dimensional array CAN be accessed by repeated use of the index notation.
requirements.original: Individual elements of multi-dimensional arrays can be accessed by repeated use of the index notation.

ambiguity.issue: Source unit is classified as example-text by the PDF conversion although it is normative prose following an example; normative is set to false per extraction rules.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: An array or record of integer restricted to a single size MAY be used in the index notation as a short-hand for the repeated index notation.
requirements.original: An array or record of integer restricted to a single size can be used in the index notation as a short-hand for the repeated index notation.

readings: An integer array or record of integer with a fixed length MAY be used as index, its length being equal to the number of indexed dimensions.
An integer array or record of integer with a fixed length not exceeding the number of dimensions MAY be used as index, yielding an array slice.

requirements.condition: the array dimension is specified using a range

requirements.subject: ent:array
requirements.canonical: An array type with a variable number of elements CANNOT be defined.
requirements.original: NOTE: It is not possible to define an array type with a variable amount of elements.

requirements.subject: ent:array
requirements.canonical: An unlimited array with a lower bound on the array index CANNOT be defined.
requirements.original: Neither is it possible to define an unlimited array with a lower bound on the array index.

requirements.subject: ent:array-element
requirements.canonical: The value of an array element SHALL be compatible with the corresponding variable or type declaration.

requirements.original: For assigning values to multi-dimensional arrays, each dimension that is assigned shall resolve to a set of values enclosed in curly braces.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep MAY be activated as a default to capture recurring behaviour.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 allows the activation of altsteps (see clause 16.2.1) as defaults to capture recurring behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:default-reference
requirements.canonical: A default reference IS a unique reference to an activated default.
requirements.original: Default references are unique references to activated defaults.

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: A test component SHALL generate a unique default reference when an altstep is activated as a default.
requirements.original: Such a unique default reference is generated by a test component when an altstep is activated as a default, i.e. a default reference is the result of an activate operation (see clause 20.5.2).

requirements.subject: ent:default-reference
requirements.canonical: A default reference IS the result of an `activate` operation.
requirements.original: Such a unique default reference is generated by a test component when an altstep is activated as a default, i.e. a default reference is the result of an activate operation (see clause 20.5.2).

requirements.subject: ent:default-reference
requirements.canonical: A default reference IS of the special predefined type `default`.
requirements.original: Default references have the special and predefined type default.

requirements.subject: ent:variable
requirements.canonical: A variable of type `default` MAY be used to handle activated defaults in a test component.
requirements.original: Variables of type default can be used to handle activated defaults in test components.

requirements.subject: ent:null-value
requirements.canonical: The special value `null` IS an unspecific default reference.
requirements.original: The special value null represents an unspecific default reference, e.g. can be used for the initialization of variables of default type.

requirements.subject: ent:null-value
requirements.canonical: The special value `null` MAY be used for the initialization of a variable of type `default`.
requirements.original: The special value null represents an unspecific default reference, e.g. can be used for the initialization of variables of default type.

requirements.subject: ent:default-reference
requirements.canonical: A default reference IS used in a `deactivate` operation to identify the default to be deactivated.
requirements.original: Default references are used in deactivate operations (see clause 20.5.3) in order to identify the default to be deactivated.

requirements.subject: ent:default-reference
requirements.canonical: A default reference IS meaningful only within the test component instance in which the default was activated.
requirements.original: Default references have meaning only within the test component instances they are activated, i.e. a default reference assigned to a default variable in test component instance "a1" of type "A" has no meaning in test component instance "a2" of type "A".

readings: Using a default reference in a test component instance other than the one where it was activated has no effect.
Using a default reference in a test component instance other than the one where it was activated SHALL cause an error.
ambiguity.issue: "has no meaning" does not state the observable consequence of using a default reference in another test component instance; no error behaviour is assumed in the canonical text.

requirements.subject: ent:test-system
requirements.canonical: The actual data representation of the `default` type SHALL be resolved externally by the test system.
requirements.original: The actual data representation of the default type shall be resolved externally by the test system.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-language
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language IS NOT restricting the implementation of a test system with respect to the handling and identification of defaults.
requirements.original: This allows abstract test cases to be specified independently of any real TTCN-3 runtime environment, in other words TTCN-3 does not restrict the implementation of a test system with respect to the handling and identification of defaults.

requirements.subject: ent:default-type
requirements.canonical: A value of the `default` type IS an object reference and follows the rules for object references.
requirements.original: Values of the default type are object references and follow specific rules for this kind of values.
